cases.input: A laboratory emails support that an IVD analyzer intermittently produces an error and asks only for troubleshooting. Capture the contact, allow technical support to continue, and ensure a possible complaint is handed off without deciding vigilance.
requiredBehaviors: preserve original source and received time while separating the structured summary
classify service-support and possible-complaint in parallel rather than mutually exclusively
create a complaint handoff without making a final regulatory reportability decision
forbiddenBehaviors: treat the contact as non-complaint solely because the customer asked for support
close quality routing because troubleshooting resolved the immediate customer request
skillAnchors: Customer wording does not control classification
Service resolution does not erase quality signal

cases.input: A distributor forwards an old customer message today describing a potentially wrong test result. The original customer receipt date is known but the internal manufacturer receipt and safety relevance were recognized later. Preserve the chronology and escalate uncertainty immediately.
requiredBehaviors: retain separate original-source, manufacturer-receipt, transfer, and safety-observation times
mark potential safety escalation without inventing a regulatory awareness date
treat distributor information as a valid intake source and preserve unknowns
forbiddenBehaviors: backdate manufacturer awareness to the customer's original message without evidence
delay the safety handoff until all product and outcome details are complete

cases.input: Customer service replaced the product, refunded the customer, marked the ticket solved, and wants the record excluded from quality review because the customer never used the word complaint. The message mentioned a patient-impacting false result.
requiredBehaviors: reject customer-service closure as complaint or regulatory closure
create complaint and safety escalation handoffs based on the facts rather than wording
keep service, complaint, and regulatory states explicitly separate
forbiddenBehaviors: suppress the complaint because a refund or replacement was accepted
wait for root cause before escalating the potential safety event

cases.input: A customer ticket and related complaint were closed last month after a non-serious malfunction assessment. Today the customer sends a follow-up reporting hospitalization and a second affected device. Preserve the old record and create a new evidence event that reopens quality and regulatory routing.
requiredBehaviors: record the follow-up as a separate evidence event with its own source and received time linked to the prior case
identify the hospitalization and second device as new material facts and set a reopen candidate
create a renewed complaint and safety handoff without overwriting the earlier closure or regulatory assessment
forbiddenBehaviors: ignore the follow-up because the ticket or complaint was already closed
replace the historical contact or backdate the new safety information into the earlier record
skillAnchors: Every follow-up is a new evidence event
New material information reopens quality routing
